assumptions: H1 (reporter module): GFP is a fourth transcriptional unit transcribed from the TetR-repressible promoter PLtetO1 with the same Hill-type repression function as the repressilator genes; its maximal strength alpha_g is set equal to the repressilator promoter strength alpha = 30 and its leakiness alpha_g0 = 0.03 (same 1e-3 ratio). These two values are ASSUMPTIONS, not measured in the paper.

H2 (growth dilution): cell growth and division are represented as a first-order dilution term mu*p acting on every protein species, with mu = ln2/60 min = 0.01155 min^-1 (doubling time 60 min, consistent with the 50-70 min division times reported). The published Box 1 model has no dilution term; this term and its value are our hypothesis.
H3: the quoted half-lives (10 min for ssrA-tagged repressors, 90 min for GFP-aav) are treated as pure degradation rates, so degradation and dilution add; this mildly overestimates total protein loss.

H4: Box 1 rescaled concentration units are retained (protein in units of K_M = 40 monomers per cell; mRNA divided by translation efficiency = 20 proteins/transcript), but time is kept in minutes (gamma_m = ln2/2 min) so that the simulated period can be compared directly with the measured 160 +/- 40 min.
H5: no repressor dimerization, no non-Hill repression curve, no mRNA dilution term, no GFP chromophore maturation step, no stochasticity.
H6: total per-cell fluorescence is proportional to p_gfp (linear read-out).

H7 (numerical): the paper does not state the initial conditions; we use a small asymmetric perturbation (m_lacI, m_tetR, m_cI) = (1, 0.3, 0), (p_lacI, p_tetR, p_cI) = (0.2, 0.05, 0), m_gfp = p_gfp = 0, because the fully symmetric initial condition is invariant and would not reveal the limit cycle.
description: Hypothesis-driven extension of the published repressilator model (Elowitz & Leibler 2000, Box 1). The core six ODEs are kept, and two mechanisms that the paper describes biologically but never formalises are added: (i) dilution of all protein species by cell growth and division, and (ii) the GFP reporter module (PLtetO1-driven gfp-aav) that produces the experimentally observed fluorescence read-out. Time is in minutes so the simulated period can be compared directly with the measured 160 +/- 40 min period. Model question: do sustained oscillations survive growth dilution, and how faithfully does the slow (90 min half-life) GFP reporter track the TetR dynamics?
missing_information: Reporter-plasmid promoter strength/copy number: alpha_g is assumed equal to alpha = 30 (the reporter plasmid is a higher-copy ColE1 plasmid, so it may in fact be stronger).
GFP chromophore oxidation/maturation rate not quantified in the paper; no maturation delay is modelled.
Calibration between arbitrary fluorescence units and GFP molecules per cell is absent, so p_gfp is only a relative read-out.
Initial conditions of the experiments and of the Fig. 1c integration are not given.
Dependence of the growth-dilution term on the actual growth law (exponential vs linear, entry into stationary phase) is not specified.
No experimental measurement of absolute repressor concentrations per cell.
model_name: Repressilator + GFP reporter read-out with growth dilution (self-derived extension of Elowitz & Leibler 2000 Box 1)

assumptions: H1 reporter module: GFP is transcribed from PLtetO1 (repressed by TetR) with the same Hill form as the repressilator genes; alpha_g = 30 and alpha_g0 = 0.03 are ASSUMED, not measured in the paper.
H2 growth dilution: first-order dilution mu*p on all proteins with mu = ln2/60 min (ASSUMED value; absent from the published model).
H3: quoted half-lives treated as pure degradation, so degradation + dilution add.
H4: Box 1 concentration rescaling retained, time kept in minutes via gamma_m = ln2/2 min.
H5: no dimerization, no non-Hill repression, no mRNA dilution, no GFP maturation, no stochasticity.
origin.source_text: self-derived from Elowitz M.B. & Leibler S., 'A synthetic oscillatory network of transcriptional regulators', Nature 403, 335-338 (2000) - mechanistic description of the PLtetO1-gfp-aav reporter, ssrA-tagged destabilised repressors and cell division; the paper does not formalise the reporter or the growth-dilution term
